Closing the loop: maximize S[p] and get p_i = B(E_i)/Z back.

Source: R/maxent.R
maxent-overview.Rd

This is the paper's central claim: the chain B -> s~(E) -> s(B) -> S[p] reconstructs an entropy from a prescribed statistical factor, and maximizing that entropy under the standard constraints (normalization and mean energy, no escort probabilities) returns the distribution started from. This closes every link at once: the branch assignment, the omega-versus-a bookkeeping, the gauge alpha=-1, and the 1/Z scaling – the highest-value regression test in the package.

Details

The gradient is exact and cheap: differentiating S[p] = sum_j Z^{-1} s(Z p_j) gives s'(Z p_i) = alpha + beta0*E(Z p_i), so the derivative of the entropy is the inverse function E(B) – no numerical differentiation needed.
